content.text: Luk Fu (å…­è™Ž), literally 'Six Tigers', is a traditional Hakka Chinese trick-taking game played with a unique money-suited deck of 38 cards. It is a highly complex and fast-paced game where players compete to be the first to capture six 'Fu' (tigers/tricks). The game features 'Aged Cards' (cards that become unbeatable) and special multi-trick combinations like 'Five Tigers Emerge From the Mountain' (Ng Fu Ha San).
Dates back centuries to the Hakka people in Southern China. It is related to other money-suited games like Khanhoo and Madiao.
3 active players (one can be a dummy dealer in a 4-player game).
38 cards: 4 suits (Coins, Strings, Myriads, Tens). Each suit has 1-9. Plus special Aces.
Chinese money-suited deck and score counters.
Each player receives 12 cards (in a 3-player game).

items.text: Four-Player Luk Fu: One player pays but does not play.
Small Fu: A variant requiring only 5 tricks.
Hakka Lucky Tiger: A gambling-heavy variant.
